cards.details: Establishment of village-based animal husbandry (cattle, sheep, goat) alongside early agricultural expansion. Development of pastoral-nomadic seasonal networks in Gujarat and Baluchistan.

Intensive cattle breeding for urban traction (carts) and dairy. Advanced riverine and marine fishing networks (Makran coast dried fish trade). Prolific animal representation in seals, copper plates, and terracotta art.
Weakening monsoons and desiccation of pastures lead to ruralization. Increased reliance on local cattle and sheep breeding, and shift towards localized, opportunistic hunting/fishing.

items.question: Which animal is most frequently depicted on Mature Harappan seals?
items.answer: The mythical Unicorn (one-horned creature), followed by the humped bull (zebu), elephant, rhinoceros, tiger, and water buffalo.

items.question: Which major domesticate is economically vital but completely absent from seal iconography?
items.answer: The Cow. Humped bulls are highly prominent, but the female cow is never depicted on seals, possibly due to taboos or specific symbolic conventions.

items.question: Where is the site of Surkotada located, and what is its faunal significance?
items.answer: Located in Gujarat. It has yielded disputed bone remains of the true horse (Equus caballus) from Mature-Late Harappan levels.

items.question: What evidence exists for the domestic cat in the Indus Valley?
items.answer: At Chanhudaro, a baked brick was found with paw prints of a dog chasing a cat, confirming their presence in urban households.

items.question: How did coastal Harappans utilize marine resources?
items.answer: They engaged in extensive sea fishing. Salted and dried marine fish were traded from coastal outposts in Baluchistan (Makran coast) to inland cities like Harappa.

sections.title: 1. Pastoral Economy and Domesticated Animals
sections.content:
Animal husbandry was a cornerstone of the Harappan subsistence economy, complementing agriculture and providing vital secondary products.

Core Domesticates & Economic Roles
  • Cattle (Bos indicus): The humped bull (zebu) was highly prized for pulling solid-wheeled carts and heavy wooden ploughshares. Cattle also provided milk, butter, and beef.
  • Small Ruminants: Sheep and goats were kept in large numbers for meat, milk, and wool. Pigs (Sus scrofa) were reared in urban dump yards for meat.
  • Beasts of Burden: Domestic asses (donkeys) and camels (bones found at Kalibangan) served as beasts of burden for overland desert trade routes.
Symbolic Representations & Taboos
  • Bull Cult: The humped bull is realistically rendered in masterfully carved steatite seals and clay figurines, indicating its status as a symbol of power or fertility.
  • The Missing Cow: Intriguingly, the female cow is completely absent from seals, copper tablets, and terracotta art. This suggests the cow was not a central ritual icon, unlike in the Rigvedic period.
  • Domestic Pets: Dogs and cats were kept. Dogs are represented in terracotta toys (some with collars), and cat footprints are recorded.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following was the most economically dominant domesticated animal in the Harappan civilization?
masteryZone.sol: Cattle (zebu) bones represent the largest percentage of faunal remains at almost all sites.

masteryZone.q: Significant remains of camel bones, indicating their domestic use for transport, have been discovered at which site?
masteryZone.sol: Kalibangan in Rajasthan has yielded significant camel bones, representing adaptation to dry environments.

masteryZone.q: The practice of burying a domestic dog alongside a human in a grave is unique to which site in the Harappan context?
masteryZone.sol: Ropar (Punjab) yielded a unique co-burial of a dog with a human, showing localized ritual practices.

masteryZone.q: Which domestic animal is completely absent from Mature Harappan seals despite its economic presence?
masteryZone.sol: The humped bull is prominent on seals, but the female cow is completely absent from all seals.

masteryZone.q: A footprint of a dog chasing a cat on a wet clay brick was excavated at which manufacturing center?
masteryZone.sol: Chanhudaro has yielded a brick with paw prints of a dog chasing a cat, indicating domestic pets.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following animals were domesticated by the Harappans for traction and burden? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Zebu, buffalo, and ass were domesticated and used for work. African elephants were not domesticated.

masteryZone.q: Select the ruminants reared by Harappans for wool, milk, and meat: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Sheep and goats were reared for wool, milk, and meat. Pigs were kept for meat but not wool. Dogs were pets.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following animals are NEVER depicted on Harappan seals? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Cow, horse, and camel are never depicted on Harappan seals. Rhinoceros is depicted.

masteryZone.q: Choose the sites that have yielded camel bones or teeth remains: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Camels were used in plains and dry regions, with bones found at Kalibangan, Harappa, and Mohenjo-daro.

masteryZone.q: Select the domestic pets whose skeletal or footprint remains have been verified in urban Harappan contexts: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Dogs and cats are well-documented. Mongoose and lions were not domestic pets.

masteryZone.q: Why is the humped bull depicted so realistically on Harappan seals while other animals are stylized?
masteryZone.sol: The humped bull held high symbolic, economic, and potentially sacred value as a draft animal, representing physical power and agricultural fertility.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Harappans avoid depicting the cow on seals despite its economic importance?
masteryZone.sol: The cow's absence was likely due to specific artistic/symbolic conventions or taboos that reserved seal iconography for powerful wild animals, mythical creatures, and draft bulls.

masteryZone.q: Why were donkeys and camels essential for the Harappan regional trade network?
masteryZone.sol: They were adapted for overland travel in arid and rocky regions (like Baluchistan and Rajasthan) where wheeled bullock carts were inefficient.

masteryZone.q: How did cattle traction transform Harappan agricultural productivity?
masteryZone.sol: By enabling the use of heavy wooden ploughshares to deep-cultivate hard alluvial clays and transport huge agrarian surpluses in wheeled carts to cities.

masteryZone.q: How do the dog-human co-burials at Ropar help reconstruct Harappan domestic relations?
masteryZone.sol: They suggest close emotional bonds between owners and dogs, and indicate localized beliefs in the afterlife where pets accompanied owners.

masteryZone.q: How did pastoral nomads interact with settled urban populations in the Indus Valley?
masteryZone.sol: They migrated seasonally, supplying cities with milk, wool, leather, and draft animals in exchange for agricultural grains and metal tools.

masteryZone.q: Analyze Kalibangan's camel bone assemblage and its implications for overland trade.
masteryZone.sol: Significant camel bones at Kalibangan indicate the animal was integrated into the local economy of northern Rajasthan, facilitating trade across the desert Thar zone.

masteryZone.q: Evaluate the Chanhudaro dog-and-cat brick paw prints as a source of domestic life history.
masteryZone.sol: The overlapping prints on a wet, unbaked clay brick suggest that dogs and cats freely roamed the streets and workshops of Chanhudaro before the brick was placed in a kiln.

masteryZone.q: Examine Ropar's domestic pet burial and its significance in Neolithic-Harappan transitions.
masteryZone.sol: The dog-human co-burial at Ropar reflects localized Neolithic cultural legacies that persisted into the Harappan phase, distinct from mainstream urban burial rites.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of 'Secondary Products Revolution' in the context of Harappan cattle husbandry.
masteryZone.sol: The use of cattle not just for meat (primary), but for secondary resources like milk, butter, and traction power (ploughing, carts) which multiplied agricultural output.

masteryZone.q: Describe the mechanism of seasonal transhumance among Harappan pastoralists in Gujarat.
masteryZone.sol: Pastoral groups moved herds between wet upland pastures during dry monsoons and dry lowland areas when water was available, trading along the route.

masteryZone.q: Explain the domestic waste cycle involving pigs in Harappan urban centers.
masteryZone.sol: Pigs acted as organic waste consumers in dump yards, helping clean cities of refuse, while providing a cheap protein source for lower-status urban populations.

sections.title: 2. Wild Animals, Hunting, and Fishing
sections.content:
Harappan society interacted extensively with wild fauna for supplementary nutrition, bone/ivory raw materials, and symbolic art.

Wild Fauna & Artistic Depictions
  • Rainforest Fauna: Tigers, elephants, rhinoceroses, and gaur (bison) are frequently depicted on seals, indicating that the Indus plain was wetter and more heavily forested than it is today.
  • The Missing Lion: The lion is extremely rare on seals (only depicted as a combat motif under Western Asian influence), whereas the tiger is a common motif, highlighting differences from Mesopotamian art.
  • Deer & Gharial: Various deer (sambar, chital, barasingha) and gharials (crocodiles) are depicted, showing familiarity with riverine and forest ecology.
Hunting, Fishing & Marine Trade
  • Hunting: Copper arrowheads and clay slingshots were used to hunt wild boar, deer, and birds. Ivory was harvested from elephants for crafting luxury pins, combs, and dice.
  • Fishing: Copper/bronze fish hooks have been excavated in large numbers at Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, and Lothal. Riverine catfish and marine fish were caught.
  • Makran Coast Fish Trade: Zooarchaeological studies of dried fish bones at Harappa show they were imported from the Makran coast, proving a structured inland-maritime trade network.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following wild felines is frequently represented on Harappan seals, whereas the lion is absent?
masteryZone.sol: The tiger is frequently depicted on seals, whereas the lion is absent or extremely rare in Mature Harappan art.

masteryZone.q: Copper/bronze fish hooks have been excavated in large numbers at which major riverine and coastal sites?
masteryZone.sol: Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, and Lothal have yielded numerous copper fish hooks, confirming active fishing industries.

masteryZone.q: The trade of salted and dried marine fish to inland cities like Harappa originated from which coastal outpost?
masteryZone.sol: Faunal remains at Harappa show marine catfish bones imported from the Makran coast of Baluchistan.

masteryZone.q: Which wild animal is depicted on the 'Pashupati Seal' alongside the elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo?
masteryZone.sol: The Pashupati seal depicts a tiger, an elephant, a rhinoceros, a buffalo, and two deer below the throne.

masteryZone.q: The Harappans harvested ivory for making combs, pins, and gaming pieces from which native animal?
masteryZone.sol: Ivory was obtained from the native Indian elephant (Elephas maximus), either hunted or kept.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following wild animals are commonly represented on steatite Harappan seals? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Tiger, rhinoceros, and elephant are common seal motifs. The lion is absent or extremely rare.

masteryZone.q: Select the materials used by Harappans for hunting wild animals and birds: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Copper arrowheads, terracotta pellets, and chert knives were used. Iron was unknown.

masteryZone.q: Which coastal sites acted as shell-processing centers for bangle manufacture? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Nageshwar (Gujarat) and Balakot (Pakistan) were major coastal centers for shell bangle manufacture. Shortughai and Kalibangan are inland.

masteryZone.q: Select the wild deer species identified from bone fragments at Harappan sites: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Chital, Sambar, and Barasingha were native to the Indus basin. Reindeer are arctic.

masteryZone.q: Choose the aquatic resources exploited by the Harappans: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: River catfish, marine shells/oysters, and river turtles were consumed. Whales were not exploited.

masteryZone.q: The lion is frequently represented on Mature Harappan seals.
masteryZone.sol: The lion is absent or extremely rare on seals.

masteryZone.q: Copper arrowheads were used by the Harappans to hunt wild game.
masteryZone.sol: Copper arrowheads have been excavated at many sites.

masteryZone.q: The chank shell (Turbinella pyrum) was harvested to manufacture bangles.
masteryZone.sol: This shell species was widely used for bangle craft.

masteryZone.q: Dried marine fish trade existed between Baluchistan coast and inland Harappa.
masteryZone.sol: Faunal remains confirm Makran coast fish bones at Harappa.

masteryZone.q: Rhinoceros depictions on seals suggest a wet, humid environment in ancient times.
masteryZone.sol: The rhino requires wet, swampy grass zones to survive.

masteryZone.q: Iron fish hooks were the primary tools used for riverine fishing.
masteryZone.sol: Iron was unknown; fish hooks were made of copper and bronze.

masteryZone.q: Pashupati seal depicts a lion seated beneath the throne.
masteryZone.sol: It depicts two deer below the throne, no lion.

masteryZone.q: Elephants were depicted on seals, indicating their native status.
masteryZone.sol: The elephant is depicted on many Mature seals and bones are found.

masteryZone.sol: The tiger is common, whereas the lion is missing.

masteryZone.q: Fish hooks found at Mohenjo-daro were manufactured using ________.
masteryZone.sol: Copper and bronze were the primary metals used.

masteryZone.q: The marine shell harvested at Nageshwar for bangle making is scientifically named ________.
masteryZone.sol: Turbinella pyrum is the chank shell used for bangles.

masteryZone.q: Ancient dried fish bones found at Harappa were imported from the ________ coast.
masteryZone.sol: The Makran coast of Baluchistan was the source.

masteryZone.sol: Ivory was a major raw material for luxury crafts.

masteryZone.sol: Clay pellets were used in slingshots for hunting.

masteryZone.sol: Tiger and elephant are depicted on the right side of the deity.

masteryZone.q: Why did marine fish trade reach deep inland cities like Harappa?
masteryZone.sol: The high food demand of urban elites and a preference for marine catfish proteins prompted a well-organized logistics network using salted and dried preservation.

masteryZone.q: How did Harappan artisans manufacture bangles and inlay work from marine shells?
masteryZone.sol: By using bronze saws to cut the shell whorls, grinding the edges with stone abrasives, and drilling holes with specialized copper drills.

masteryZone.q: How did the preservation of marine fish enable long-distance trade to inland centers?
masteryZone.sol: Fish were gutted, salted, and sun-dried along the Makran coast to prevent decay during the multi-week transport to inland Punjab.

masteryZone.q: How was elephant ivory harvested and processed in urban workshops?
masteryZone.sol: Tusks were cut into blanks using fine metal saws, then carved, incised, and polished in specialized urban workshops like the one at Lothal.

masteryZone.q: Analyze the faunal findings at Balakot and their implications for coastal resource consumption.
masteryZone.sol: Balakot yielded massive piles of shell debitage and marine fish bones, proving coastal populations relied almost entirely on marine harvesting rather than land farming.

masteryZone.q: Examine the ivory workshop discoveries at Lothal as evidence of urban craft organization.
masteryZone.sol: The Lothal ivory workshop has yielded raw tusks, waste chips, and finished combs, demonstrating a high degree of division of labor and craft specialization.

masteryZone.q: Examine the Pashupati seal as a visual catalog of the Mature Harappan wild ecosystem.
masteryZone.sol: The inclusion of rhino, elephant, tiger, and buffalo on a single seal represents a wet, high-rainfall forest ecology, proving Kutch and Sindh were humid zones.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of 'Resource Proximity' in Harappan shell working industries.
masteryZone.sol: Workshops were situated directly on the coast (Nageshwar, Balakot) to minimize transport of heavy, raw marine shells, exporting only light finished bangles inland.

masteryZone.q: Describe the ecological significance of the 'Forest Fauna Suite' in reconstructive archaeology.
masteryZone.sol: The presence of tigers, rhinos, and elephants on seals tells us the ancient Indus valley had tall grasslands and riverine gallery forests, indicating high monsoonal rainfall.

masteryZone.q: Explain the dried-fish logistics trade between the Makran coast and inland Punjab.
masteryZone.sol: Coastal communities caught marine catfish, cured them using salt, dried them, and packed them into containers to be shipped via rivers and land routes to Mohenjo-daro and Harappa.

sections.title: 3. Zooarchaeology and The Horse Controversy
sections.content:
Scientific analysis of bone remains (osteology) helps reconstruct dietary habits, pastoral management, and long-standing historical debates.

Zooarchaeological Methods & Bone Data
  • Cut Marks: High concentrations of bones with cut marks near urban residential sectors prove meat processing and butchery.
  • Mortality Profiles: The slaughter of sheep/goats at young ages indicates meat production, whereas keeping cattle to old age indicates they were used for milk and traction.
  • Wild vs Domestic: Domesticated cattle, buffalo, sheep, and goat bones make up over 70% to 80% of faunal assemblages at most sites, proving that hunting was secondary.
The Surkotada Horse Controversy
  • Surkotada Bones: Excavated by J.P. Joshi, Mature-Late Harappan layers yielded bones claimed to be the true horse (Equus caballus). Archaeologist Sandor Bokonyi confirmed this identification.
  • The Counter-Argument: Other scholars, including Richard Meadow, argue these bones belong to the wild ass (khur/Equus hemionus) or domestic ass, which are native to Kutch.
  • Vedic Shift: The horse is central to Rigvedic culture but completely absent from Harappan seals and terracotta art (unlike the bull/unicorn). Therefore, it was not culturally integrated into Harappan society.

masteryZone.q: The controversial skeletal remains of a horse, claimed by Sandor Bokonyi to belong to Equus caballus, were found at which site?
masteryZone.sol: Surkotada in Gujarat yielded disputed horse bones from Mature-Late Harappan levels.

masteryZone.q: Who is the primary zooarchaeologist who challenged the Surkotada horse identification, attributing the bones to the wild ass?
masteryZone.sol: Richard Meadow argued that the bones belonged to the wild ass (Equus hemionus) or domestic donkey, native to Kutch.

masteryZone.q: The native wild ass of the Rann of Kutch, often confused with the horse in bone studies, is scientifically named:
masteryZone.sol: The wild ass (khur) is scientifically known as Equus hemionus.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following sites has yielded dental remains (teeth) controversially attributed to the horse?
masteryZone.sol: Kalibangan in Rajasthan has yielded teeth remains attributed to the Equidae family (ass/horse).

masteryZone.q: The complete absence of which animal on Mature Harappan seals is a major argument against its cultural integration?
masteryZone.sol: The horse is completely missing from all Harappan seals, unlike the humped bull, tiger, and rhino.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following sites have yielded skeletal fragments or clay models associated with the horse/ass debate? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Surkotada (bones), Lothal (figurine), and Kalibangan (teeth) are involved. Nageshwar has no horse remains.

masteryZone.q: Select the key arguments used by scholars who reject horse domestication in Harappa: (Select all that apply)
opts: Complete absence of horse depictions on seals
Surkotada bones belong to the native wild ass (Equus hemionus)
True horses only entered the subcontinent with Rigvedic people

masteryZone.sol: The absence on seals, structural similarity to wild ass, and Vedic migrations are key arguments. Bones have been claimed, so option 3 is false.

masteryZone.q: What features distinguish the Equus hemionus (wild ass) from the Equus caballus (true horse) in bone anatomy? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Metapodials and molar enamel foldings are key diagnostic criteria in equine osteology. Equines do not have horns.

masteryZone.q: Select the domestic ruminants whose mortality profiles indicate milk/wool production rather than immediate meat slaughter: (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Adult cattle (traction/milk) and adult sheep (wool) survived to old ages. Young lambs and pigs were slaughtered for meat.

masteryZone.q: Choose the scientific methods used in zooarchaeology to analyze Harappan animal bones: (Select all that apply)
opts: DNA profiling of ancient pottery residue
masteryZone.sol: Osteology, cut-mark micro-analysis, and age profiles are faunal methods. Pottery residue is lipid/chemical analysis.

masteryZone.sol: Equus caballus is the biological classification of the horse.

masteryZone.sol: Horse bones are extremely rare/disputed; camel bones are more documented but still limited.

masteryZone.sol: The vast majority of bone fragments belong to domestic species, proving pastoral dominance.

masteryZone.sol: Kalibangan yielded equid teeth remains.

masteryZone.sol: Zooarchaeology (or faunal analysis) is the scientific study of animal remains.

masteryZone.sol: Cut marks indicate butchering for food consumption.

masteryZone.q: Why are equid bone identifications so controversial in Harappan archaeology?
masteryZone.sol: Because the skeletal structures of horses, domestic asses, and native wild asses (khur) are extremely similar, and Kutch is home to native wild asses, causing potential misidentifications.

masteryZone.q: Why did the absence of horse representations on seals influence the Aryan invasion debate?
masteryZone.sol: The horse is central to Rigvedic culture. Its absence from Harappan seals suggests that the Indus civilization was culturally distinct and predated the horse-centric Vedic culture.

masteryZone.q: Why do zooarchaeologists compile mortality profiles of sheep and goat bones?
masteryZone.sol: To determine pastoral strategies: slaughtering young animals suggests meat production, whereas keeping mature ones suggests milk or wool harvesting.

masteryZone.q: How do zooarchaeologists distinguish cut marks caused by bronze tools from carnivore gnawing?
masteryZone.sol: By analyzing the cuts under high magnification; bronze tools create clean, V-shaped grooves with parallel striations, while teeth create shallow, U-shaped scrapes.

masteryZone.q: How did Sandor Bokonyi identify the Surkotada bones as Equus caballus?
masteryZone.sol: By conducting metric measurements of the metapodials and checking enamel folding patterns on the molars, which matched true horse references.

masteryZone.q: How does bone chemistry (stable isotope analysis) help reconstruct Harappan animal diets?
masteryZone.sol: By analyzing carbon and nitrogen isotopes in bone collagen, which reveals whether the animals fed on plains grasses (C4 plants) or hilly shrubs (C3 plants).

masteryZone.q: Analyze the Surkotada equine bone assemblage and the debate between Bokonyi and Meadow.
masteryZone.sol: Bokonyi identified the bones as Equus caballus using metrical analysis, while Meadow challenged it as Equus hemionus, emphasizing the native presence of wild asses in Kutch.

masteryZone.q: Examine the bone refuse heaps of Mohenjo-daro as a source of urban dietary profiles.
masteryZone.sol: Residential refuse dumps at Mohenjo-daro yielded massive quantities of cattle, buffalo, and pig bones with cut marks, proving meat was a major component of the urban diet.

masteryZone.q: Evaluate the equine teeth discoveries at Kalibangan and their archaeological context.
masteryZone.sol: The equid teeth remains at Kalibangan are located in Mature Harappan layers, but due to lack of complete skeletons, their domestic horse status remains unproven.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of 'Zooarchaeology' and its role in reconstructing ancient subsistence.
masteryZone.sol: Zooarchaeology is the study of animal remains from archaeological sites to reconstruct past human diets, economies, animal domestication processes, and local environments.

masteryZone.q: Describe how bone cut-mark analysis under a Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) works.
masteryZone.sol: SEM analysis scans bone surfaces to inspect the microscopic geometry of cuts; clean V-grooves with striations verify the use of sharp metal (bronze) butchery knives.

masteryZone.q: Explain the historical significance of the 'Horse Debate' in the transition from Harappan to Vedic culture.
masteryZone.sol: The horse is a cultural marker; its absolute absence in Harappan iconography and heavy presence in Vedic texts shows that Mature Harappan cities were culturally and chronologically separate from Rigvedic society.

traps.title: UPSC Warning Alerts (Traps to Avoid)
items: Trap 1: Do not choose statements claiming that the cow was the most common animal depicted on seals. Humped bulls are common, but the cow is NEVER depicted on seals.

Trap 2: Avoid options asserting that the horse was a central draft animal in Mature Harappan chariot warfare. Light-spoked wheeled chariots and horse-drawn warfare only appear in the Vedic/Post-Vedic period.
Trap 3: Do not assume the lion was a popular icon. The lion is absent/rare on seals; the tiger is the dominant feline motif.
Trap 4: Watch out for questions claiming camels were absent. Camel bones are documented at Kalibangan and were used for desert transport.
Trap 5: Do not confuse domestic dog burials. Human burials with dogs are found at Ropar (Punjab), which is a key Neolithic-Harappan transition site.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the pastoral economy of the Indus Valley Civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. Cattle (zebu) bones represent the largest percentage of faunal remains at almost all sites.
2. Sheep and goats were reared together primarily for milk and wool.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Cattle (zebu) bones are the most dominant faunal remains (50-60%), and sheep and goats were reared in mixed herds for milk, meat, and wool.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the cow in Harappan culture:
1. Humped bulls are highly prominent on steatite administrative seals.
2. The female cow is depicted alongside the humped bull on several seals from Mohenjo-daro.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the female cow is completely absent from all known Harappan seals and iconography, which is a major contrast to the Rigvedic period.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the beasts of burden in the Harappan civilization, consider the following statements:
1. Camel bones showing adaptation to dry climates have been excavated in significant quantities at Kalibangan.
2. Camels were the primary source of traction for ploughing agricultural fields in Punjab.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: humped oxen (bulls) were the primary draft animals used for agricultural plough traction, not camels.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding burial practices in Harappan cities:
1. A human burial containing a domestic dog buried alongside the deceased was excavated at Ropar.
2. The practice of burying domestic pets with their owners was common across all major Harappan cemeteries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the dog-human co-burial is unique to Ropar in Punjab and not found in other Harappan cemeteries.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to domestic pets in the Indus Valley Civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. A wet clay brick with paw prints of a dog chasing a cat was discovered at Chanhudaro.
2. Terracotta toys of dogs showing collar bands suggest they were kept as domestic pets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Chanhudaro yielded a brick with paw prints showing a dog chasing a cat, and terracotta dog toys from Harappa show collars, proving their pet status.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the humped cattle of the Indus Valley Civilisation:
1. Humped cattle are scientifically classified as Bos indicus.
2. The humped bull or zebu is carved with great detail and artistic realism on administrative seals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Humped cattle are Bos indicus and were carved with extreme realism on steatite seals.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to overland trade networks of the Harappans, consider the following statements:
1. Domestic asses (donkeys) were used as beasts of burden for transport across rocky terrains.
2. Camel remains at Kalibangan suggest camels were utilized for desert trade routes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Donkeys and camels served as pack animals for overland trade in arid and rocky regions (Baluchistan/Rajasthan).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan diets and zooarchaeological remains:
1. High concentrations of domestic pig (Sus scrofa) bones are found in refuse heaps near urban residential sectors.
2. Pigs were kept in urban dump yards, feeding on organic waste and providing a source of meat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Pig bones are common in urban refuse middens, indicating pigs consumed organic waste and were slaughtered for meat.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan sheep and goat herding, consider the following statements:
1. Pastoral groups reared sheep and goats together in mixed herds to exploit complementary resources.
2. Sheep were sheared for wool, whereas goats were primarily kept for milk and meat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Sheep and goats were kept together; sheep provided wool, and both provided milk and meat.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding terracotta figurines in Harappan sites:
1. Toy figurines representing dogs have been excavated showing collar bands.
2. Terracotta models of horses showing spoked-wheeled chariots have been found at Mohenjo-daro.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: horses and spoked-wheeled chariots are completely absent from Harappan terracotta art.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to felines depicted in Mature Harappan art, consider the following statements:
1. The tiger is a common motif on seals, often shown in scenes with men in trees.
2. The Asiatic lion is frequently depicted on seals as a symbol of royal power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the lion is absent or extremely rare on seals, unlike the tiger which is highly common.

practiceQuestions.q:
Which of the following wild animals are depicted on the famous 'Pashupati Seal' of Mohenjo-daro?
1. Tiger
2. Elephant
3. Rhinoceros
4. Lion
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pashupati seal depicts a tiger, an elephant, a rhinoceros, and a buffalo surrounding the deity, with two deer below the throne. The lion is absent.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the representation of aquatic fauna in Harappan art:
1. The gharial or fish-eating crocodile is commonly depicted on pottery, amulets, and seals.
2. Marine fish and tortoises are depicted on painted pottery at coastal sites like Lothal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Gharials represent riverine fauna on seals/pottery, and marine species are common in coastal Lothal art.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the maritime trade of the Harappans, consider the following statements:
1. Dried and salted marine fish were traded from coastal outposts on the Makran coast to inland cities like Harappa.
2. Fish bone assemblages at Harappa include species native only to the Arabian Sea.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Zooarchaeological analysis of fish bones at Harappa shows they include marine species traded from the Makran coast (800 km away).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding fishing technology in Harappan sites:
1. Large numbers of copper and bronze fish hooks have been excavated at Mohenjo-daro and Lothal.
2. The Harappans relied exclusively on bone hooks due to the scarcity of metals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: metal hooks of copper and bronze were widely used for fishing in both rivers and seas.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the manufacturing of shell objects, consider the following statements:
1. Coastal sites like Nageshwar and Balakot specialized in the procurement and carving of marine chank shells.
2. Marine shell bangles, ladles, and inlay work were traded from coastal workshops to inland cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Nageshwar and Balakot were dedicated shell-craft centers that traded finished goods (bangles, ladles) inland.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding ivory utilization in the Indus Valley Civilisation:
1. Lothal has yielded ivory workshop remains, including unworked elephant tusks and waste flakes.
2. Ivory was exported from the Indus Valley (Meluhha) to Mesopotamia as a luxury trade commodity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Lothal has an ivory workshop, and Akkadian texts list ivory from Meluhha (Indus valley) as a premium import.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan hunting practices, consider the following statements:
1. Copper arrowheads and clay slingshots were used to hunt wild boar, deer, and birds.
2. Wild animal bones represent the main source of daily protein in large urban centers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: domesticated livestock bones make up over 80% of urban assemblages; hunting wild game was secondary.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding zooarchaeological analysis of animal bones:
1. Sharp cut marks and scrapes at joints indicate butchery and meat processing for human consumption.
2. Charring or burning of bones shows they were roasted or cooked.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Cut marks and charring are direct osteological evidence of slaughtering and cooking animals for food.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the economic use of cattle, consider the following statements:
1. Zooarchaeological mortality profiles showing cattle living to old age suggest they were used for milk and agricultural traction.
2. Cattle were slaughtered uniformly at very young ages, indicating they were raised exclusively for beef.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Keeping cattle until old age proves they were valued for their milk and labor (pulling carts/ploughs) rather than quick meat.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the herding of sheep in Harappan cities:
1. Sheep were kept to mature ages to harvest maximum wool yields over several years.
2. Woven wool and cotton textiles were primary industrial exports of the Harappans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Zooarchaeological age profiles confirm sheep were kept to mature ages to shear wool, which was woven into textiles for trade.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the site of Surkotada in Gujarat, consider the following statements:
1. J.P. Joshi excavated Mature-Late Harappan layers that yielded bones claimed to be the true horse.
2. Hungarian zooarchaeologist Sandor Bokonyi confirmed the identification of these bones as Equus caballus.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. J.P. Joshi excavated horse bones at Surkotada, and Bokonyi verified them as belonging to the true horse (Equus caballus).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the counter-arguments in the horse controversy:
1. Scholar Richard Meadow argues that the Surkotada bones belong to the wild ass (khur) or domestic donkey.
2. The wild ass (Equus hemionus) is native to the Rann of Kutch and shares skeletal similarities with the horse.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Meadow contested the horse claim, asserting the bones belong to the native wild ass (khur), which looks similar osteologically.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the cultural role of the horse, consider the following statements:
1. The horse is completely absent from all Mature Harappan seals and terracotta art.
2. The horse holds a central religious and economic place in Rigvedic culture, unlike in Harappan iconography.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The horse's absence on seals shows it was not culturally integrated in Harappa, representing a sharp shift from Vedic culture.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the environmental changes in the Late Harappan phase:
1. Disappearance of water-loving fauna like rhinoceros and elephant bones from refuse dumps indicates climatic drying.
2. Late Harappan assemblages show an increase in dry-adapted sheep and goat remains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The shift in bone assemblages from wet-climate species to dry-adapted ruminants confirms environmental desiccation around 1900 BCE.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to pastoral nomadic groups in Gujarat, consider the following statements:
1. They engaged in seasonal migrations (transhumance) between dry plains and wet hills to secure pastures.
2. They supplied urban Harappan centers with milk, wool, hides, and draft animals in exchange for grains and metal tools.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Seasonal pastoral migration (transhumance) was vital for herd survival and maintained symbiotic trade with cities.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding zooarchaeological statistics at Harappan sites:
1. Domesticated cattle, buffalo, sheep, and goat bones constitute over 70% to 80% of faunal remains at most urban sites.
2. Bones of wild deer and antelope are completely absent from all urban kitchen middens.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: wild deer bones are present, indicating supplementary hunting, though it was minor.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to coastal subsistence strategies at Balakot, consider the following statements:
1. Excavations show high consumption of marine fish and sea turtles, indicating a marine-dominant diet.
2. The site was a major center for herding humped camels for maritime shipment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Balakot was a coastal shell-craft and sea-fishing center, not a camel herding outpost.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding transportation in the Indus Valley Civilisation:
1. Terracotta toy models of carts show they were designed to be pulled by humped oxen.
2. These toy models feature solid, spoke-less clay wheels matching track ruts found in streets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Bullock carts with solid hubless wheels were the primary bulk overland transport system, as confirmed by toys and ruts.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan glyptic art, consider the following statements:
1. Seals were carved out of soft talcose rock called steatite and then fired to glaze them.
2. The humped bull or zebu was the single most common animal depicted on seals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the mythological one-horned unicorn was the most common motif, not the humped bull.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding wild fauna remains in Harappan refuse heaps:
1. Bones of rhinoceros, wild boar, and various deer species indicate supplementary hunting.
2. Wild birds like peacocks, jungle fowl, and ducks were also hunted for food.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Refuse piles yield bones of wild boar, deer, and birds, proving that hunting supplemented agricultural diets.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to Harappan seal iconography, consider the following statements:
1. Seals sometimes depict composite creatures, such as a three-headed beast combining a bull, unicorn, and ibex.
2. Human-faced quadrupeds with unicorn horns suggest complex mythological and religious beliefs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Composite and chimerical creatures are highly common on seals, indicating administrative or mythological icons.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding kitchen refuse at Harappa:
1. Heavy concentrations of river turtle shells with burn marks indicate they were boiled and consumed.
2. Turtles were kept in domestic ponds as sacred household guardians and never eaten.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: burned shell fragments prove turtles were harvested from rivers and cooked for food.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to dental remains at Kalibangan, consider the following statements:
1. Excavations yielded jaw fragments and teeth belonging to the Equidae (horse/ass) family.
2. These dental remains conclusively prove that the true domestic horse was used for agriculture in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: these teeth are highly debated and cannot conclusively differentiate between horses and asses.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding household pets in Harappan cities:
1. Terracotta figurines show dogs with collars, proving they were domesticated for guarding and companionship.
2. Domestic cats are represented by terracotta figurines showing cats catching mice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: cats are proven by brick paw prints (Chanhudaro), but cat toy figurines are extremely rare or absent.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to harvesting tools in Harappan fields, consider the following statements:
1. Chert blades set in wooden handles were the primary tools used as sickles to harvest grains.
2. Bronze and copper sickles were mass-produced in urban factories to harvest rabi crops.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: metal sickles were extremely rare, as chert (stone) was the primary material for sickles.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) in Harappa:
1. Buffaloes were domesticated and used for milk, meat, and traction in wet alluvial soils.
2. Buffalo bones show high concentrations in water-logged coastal outposts of Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The water buffalo was domesticated and exploited for dairy, meat, and traction in wet fields.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to wild birds in Harappan art, consider the following statements:
1. The peacock is frequently painted on pottery and modeled as terracotta figurines, showing its symbolic value.
2. Peacocks are depicted on seals as draft birds pulling the chariots of deities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: peacocks were never depicted as draft birds pulling chariots (chariots themselves were unknown).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding cuneiform inscriptions of Mesopotamia:
1. Tablets list ivory items imported from the land of 'Meluhha', which is identified as the Indus Valley.
2. Raw elephant tusks were shipped via Persian Gulf transit ports to Mesopotamian workshops.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Mesopotamian records list ivory objects and tusks imported from Meluhha (the Indus valley) via the Gulf.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to livestock management in rural Gujarat, consider the following statements:
1. Circular stone and brick enclosures found at rural sites functioned as corrals to pen sheep, goats, or cattle at night.
2. These enclosures were built to protect domesticated herds from wild predators like tigers and leopards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Circular corrals protect livestock from nocturnal predators, representing structured rural pastoral management.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan fishing gear:
1. Fish hooks excavated at riverine and coastal sites were made of copper and bronze.
2. Iron fish hooks were widely traded from Gangetic sites during the Mature Harappan phase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: iron was completely unknown to the Harappans, who relied on copper/bronze for metal hooks.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to ritual evidence at Harappan sites, consider the following statements:
1. Clay altars at Kalibangan containing animal bones and ash suggest cattle sacrifices.
2. The 'Pashupati Seal' depicts a deity performing a horse sacrifice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Pashupati seal shows a seated yogic figure surrounded by wild animals, not a sacrifice scene.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the contrast between Harappan and Rigvedic societies:
1. Harappan seals are dominated by bulls and unicorns, while Rigvedic culture is highly horse-centric.
2. Harappan civilization was urban and commercial, while Rigvedic society was pastoral and rural.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. These represent key differences in economy, settlement types, and faunal focus between the two periods.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the wild ass (khur) of Kutch, consider the following statements:
1. The scientific name of the wild ass is Equus hemionus.
2. Its bones are osteologically very similar to the true horse, causing identification controversies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The wild ass (Equus hemionus) is native to Kutch and its skeletal similarity to the horse fuels the Surkotada debate.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding burial offerings in Harappan graves:
1. Skeletons of domestic dogs are found in almost every single excavated Harappan grave.
2. Ropar is the only site where a dog was found buried directly beneath the owner's body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: dog co-burials are extremely rare, with Ropar being the only verified site.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the ancient environment of the Indus Valley, consider the following statements:
1. The frequent depiction of swampy species like rhinoceros and tigers on seals indicates a humid, wet climate.
2. The complete absence of desert animals like camels on seals shows the valley was completely forested.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: camels existed (proven by bones at Kalibangan) but were simply not chosen as seal motifs.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding manufacturing from wild animal remains:
1. Antlers of wild deer (sambar/chital) were collected from forests to manufacture needles, awls, and pins.
2. Antlers show signs of sawing and carving in workshops at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Deer antlers were collected and processed in urban workshops to make bone implements and tools.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the late Harappan pastoral shifts, consider the following statements:
1. The decline of urban granaries led to a decentralization of herding and local dairy production.
2. Late Harappan populations in Gujarat focused heavily on herding goats and sheep rather than large cattle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The transition to rural settings was accompanied by herding smaller, drought-adapted sheep and goats.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding buffalo representations on seals:
1. Seals sometimes depict a water buffalo in combat with a tiger, representing nature myths.
2. Buffalo horn motifs are depicted on the headgear of deities, indicating sacred value.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Buffaloes are shown in combat scenes, and horned headgear is a diagnostic feature of Harappan deities on seals.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to exchange systems in Harappan trade, consider the following statements:
1. Standardized chert weights, mostly cubic, were used to weigh commodities during barter transactions.
2. Trade of pastoral items like wool and hides relied on metallic coins with animal engravings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: coins did not exist; barter backed by standardized chert weights was the system.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the pastoral economy of the Mature Harappan Civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. Humped cattle (zebu) were the most economically dominant domesticated animals.
2. The cow is frequently depicted alongside the zebu bull on steatite administrative seals.
3. Bone cuts and scrape marks suggest that cattle were slaughtered for meat in urban centers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Cattle bones dominate faunal assemblages. Statement 2 is incorrect: The cow is completely absent from seals. Statement 3 is correct: Cut marks on cattle bones near residential sectors show meat processing and slaughter.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the wild fauna of the Indus Valley:
1. The tiger and rhinoceros are frequently depicted on seals, indicating a wet, swampy climate.
2. The lion is the most common feline depicted on Mature Harappan seals.
3. Elephant remains and ivory items indicate that elephants were native to the region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: The lion is absent or extremely rare on seals; the tiger is the dominant feline represented.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched?
Archaeological Site - Faunal Finding
1. Surkotada - Disputed skeletal remains of the true horse
2. Chanhudaro - Paw prints of a dog chasing a cat on a baked brick
3. Kalibangan - Significant remains of camel bones
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three pairs are correctly matched. Surkotada has disputed horse bones, Chanhudaro the brick print, and Kalibangan has camel bones.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to zooarchaeological studies in the Indus Valley Civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. Reconstructed age-at-death profiles of cattle show they were kept until old age, indicating dairy and traction use.
2. Sheep and goats were slaughtered at young ages, indicating meat production.
3. Wild animals represent more than 50% of the total bone assemblages at all major urban sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Domesticated animal bones constitute over 70% to 80% of assemblages at major sites; wild game represents a minor portion of the diet.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the horse remains debate in Harappan archaeology:
1. Sandor Bokonyi identified horse bones at Surkotada as belonging to Equus caballus.
2. Richard Meadow argued that the Surkotada bones belong to the wild ass (Equus hemionus) or domestic donkey.
3. The horse is a central motif on the seals of Mohenjo-daro, representing ruling class power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: The horse is completely absent from seals and terracotta art, which is a major contrast to Vedic culture.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to hunting and fishing in Harappan society, consider the following statements:
1. Copper fish hooks have been excavated at Mohenjo-daro and Lothal, proving active fishing.
2. Salted and dried marine fish were transported from the Makran coast of Baluchistan to inland cities.
3. Harappans used iron arrowheads to hunt wild boar and deer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Iron was unknown to the Harappans (Bronze Age); they used copper or chert arrowheads.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Domestic dog burials alongside humans have been excavated at Ropar in Punjab.
2. Terracotta figurines from Harappa show dogs wearing collars, suggesting they were domesticated pets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Dog-human co-burial is a unique finding at Ropar, and toy dogs show collars at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Which of the following wild animals are depicted on the famous 'Pashupati Seal' of Mohenjo-daro?
1. Tiger
2. Elephant
3. Rhinoceros
4. Lion
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Pashupati seal depicts a tiger, an elephant, a rhinoceros, and a buffalo surrounding the central deity. The lion is not depicted on the seal.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to shell and ivory processing in Harappan coastal settlements, consider the following statements:
1. Chank shell (Turbinella pyrum) was harvested at Balakot and Nageshwar to manufacture bangles.
2. Ivory workshops containing unworked elephant tusks have been excavated at Lothal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Coastal shell workshops and Lothal's ivory factory are well-documented archaeological findings.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: The transition from humped cattle representations on seals to horse representations represents the transition from Harappan to Vedic culture.
Statement 2: The Rigvedic economy was primarily pastoral and horse-centric, whereas the Mature Harappan economy was agricultural, urban, and bull-centric.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The horse-centric Rigveda is culturally distinct from the bull/unicorn-dominated iconography of the Harappan civilization.
